title: Why Does Anything Exist? The Antimatter Mystery
description:
The Big Bang should have made equal amounts of matter and antimatter, which destroy each other on contact. Yet roughly one extra particle of matter per billion survived, and it became everything we see. CP violation, first found in kaons in 1964 and seen in baryons by CERN's LHCb in 2025, is a real clue, but the effects measured so far are far too small. Why matter won is still unsolved.

CERN, Antimatter and the matter-antimatter asymmetry: https://home.cern/science/physics/antimatter
CERN, A new piece in the matter-antimatter puzzle (LHCb, 2025): https://home.cern/news/news/physics/new-piece-matter-antimatter-puzzle
Symmetry Magazine, Charge-parity violation: https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/charge-parity-violation
